prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: generated raster world-atlas artwork for a pale-blue editorial website.
Input image is a STYLE AND COMPOSITION REFERENCE: Blaeu's seventeenth-century engraved world atlas. Create a new digitally generated facsimile in that restrained copperplate engraving spirit, not a photograph of a book and not a modern flat vector infographic.
Wide landscape 3:2 canvas. Uniform very pale icy blue paper #edf6fd, restrained navy-blue #234f79 engraved coastline strokes, faint grey-blue grid. Main rectangular world map occupies approximately x 4% to 96%, y 5% to 76%; Greenwich centered. Recognizable, geographically accurate MODERN continent outlines with North America on left, Europe/Africa center, Asia/India right, Australia lower right. Use a regular longitude/latitude graticule and modern equirectangular geography; retain recognizable Great Lakes, Canadian Atlantic coast/Nova Scotia, central Europe, eastern Mediterranean and southern India.
Keep historical printed-map charm through gently irregular engraved lines, a double hairline border, sparse delicate shoreline hatching, two small circular polar globe insets beneath the main map (bottom left and bottom right), and one small compass rose at bottom centre. Do not fill continental interiors with dense engraved mountains or shading. Oceans calm and empty. No figures, no ships, no framing book or page shadows, no place names, no map title, no writing or pseudo-lettering, no city dots or connecting lines. All partner points and labels will be added separately on the website.
Most important: a beautiful airy blue engraved IMAGE with readable clean geography and a quietly tactile printed finish. Use MUCH less detail than reference, only a trace of halftone grain at edges, no heavy dithering across coastlines. Entire map and both polar globes visible with generous pale-paper breathing room.
